card: Documents that `btck_Block` instances cache context-free validation results in the libbitcoinkernel C API. Because `btck_Block` wraps a shared `CBlock` and sets `fChecked`, verifying a block under one set of consensus parameters causes subsequent validation under different parameters to skip checks and pass erroneously. This PR warns API consumers in header documentation to only evaluate a block against a single set of consensus parameters rather than altering validation behavior in code.
changed_since_previous: Switched from a code fix that created shallow unflagged copies of the block on every call to purely documentation notes in `src/kernel/bitcoinkernel.h` advising users to not reuse a block across multiple sets of consensus parameters.
evidence: PR description: 'once a block passed btck_block_check or btck_chainstate_manager_process_block, later calls on it (or on a copy) skip the checks, whatever consensus params or flags are passed. For example a regtest block that has passed once with regtest params also returns 1 from btck_block_check with mainnet params.'
problem: In `libbitcoinkernel`, `btck_Block` wraps a shared `CBlock`. Once context-free checks pass under one set of consensus parameters, `CheckBlock` sets `fChecked`, causing subsequent checks or processing calls on that block (or its copies) under different parameters to skip validation and return success without warning the API consumer.

risk.why: This is a documentation-only change to the libbitcoinkernel public header.

summary: Document in the libbitcoinkernel C API headers that `btck_Block` instances cache context-free validation results. The header comments for `btck_block_check` and `btck_chainstate_manager_process_block` now warn callers that cached checks persist across shallow copies and that a block should only be used with a single set of consensus parameters.
